chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ali ibn Hassan al-Wasiti, from his uncle Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir al-Hashimi, the mawla of Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said:

One day, the Commander of the Faithful (blessings of God upon him) was sitting with Ibn al-Hanafiyya when he said: O Muhammad, bring me a vessel of water so that I may perform ablution for prayer. So Muhammad brought him the water. He poured with his right hand over his left hand, then said: In the name of God. Praise be to God who made water pure and did not make it impure.

Then he performed istinja and said: O God, fortify my private parts and keep them chaste, cover my private areas, and forbid me from the Fire. Then he rinsed his mouth and said: O God, make me utter my proof on the Day I meet You, and make my tongue free in Your remembrance. Then he rinsed his nose and said: O God, do not deprive me of the fragrance of Paradise, and make me of those who smell its fragrance, its coolness, and its sweetness.

Then he washed his face and said: O God, whiten my face on the Day when faces are blackened, and do not blacken my face on the Day when faces are whitened. Then he washed his right hand and said: O God, give me my Book in my right hand and eternity in the Gardens in my left hand, and reckon me with an easy reckoning. Then he washed his left hand and said: O God, do not give me my Book in my left hand, and do not bind it to my neck; and I seek refuge in You from the fire-cuttings.

Then he wiped his head and said: O God, envelop me in Your mercy, Your blessings, and Your pardon. Then he wiped his feet and said: O God, make my feet firm upon the Bridge on the Day when feet slip from it, and direct my striving toward what pleases You on my behalf. Then he raised his head, looked at Muhammad, and said: O Muhammad, whoever performs ablution like my ablution and says what I have said, God, Mighty and Majestic, will create from every drop an angel who glorifies Him, praises Him, and magnifies Him; and God, Mighty and Majestic, will record its reward for him until the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.الاستنجاء: Istinja — ritual purification of the private parts after relieving oneself
key_terms.الخلد في الجنان: Eternity in the Gardens — perpetual dwelling in Paradise
key_terms.الصراط: al-Sirat — the Bridge over Hell that all must cross on the Day of Resurrection
key_terms.الوضوء: Wudu — ritual ablution before prayer, purifying specific limbs
key_terms.مقطعات النيران: Muqatti'at al-niran — cutting portions of Hellfire, meaning punishing fire

ai.seo_question: What are the supplications Imam Ali recited during wudu?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and traced back to Imam Ali (AS), describes in detail the wudu (ritual ablution) performed by the Commander of the Faithful in the presence of his son Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya, with specific supplications for each step of the ablution. Each act of purification is paired with an eschatological prayer — purifying the face is matched with a prayer for it to be illuminated on the Day of Judgment, washing the hands with a prayer for receiving one's record in the right hand, and so forth. The hadith concludes with the promise that anyone who performs wudu in this manner will have an angel created from every drop of water, whose continuous glorification of God will be recorded for the worshiper until the Day of Resurrection.
word_analysis: so that I may perform ablution

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from `Ali b. Hassan al-Wasiti from his uncle `Abd al-Rahman b. Kathir al-Hashimi the servant of Muhammad b. `Ali from Abi `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as). He said:

One day, Amir al-Mu’minin (as) was sitting with Ibn Hanafiyya when he said: O Muhammad! Bring me a vessel of water so that I may perform ablution for prayer. So, Muhammad brought him water. Then, he placed his right hand on his left hand and said: In the name of Allah. Praise be to Allah who made water pure and did not make it impure (bismillah walhamdu lillahil lathi ja`alal ma’a tahuran wa lam yaj`alhu najisa).

He said: Then, he washed his private and said: O Allah! Protect my private and purify it, cover my private, and forbid me from the Fire (Allahumma hassin farji wa a`ifahu wastur `awrati wa harrimni `alal nar). He said: Then, he rinsed his mouth and said: O Allah! Make me meet my proof on the day I meet You, and make my tongue speak in Your remembrance (Allahumma laqini hujati yawma alqaka wa atliq lisani bi dhikrika). Then, he rinsed his nose and said: O Allah! Do not forbid me from the fragrance of Paradise, and make me of those who smell its fragrance, its rest, and its sweetness (Allahumma la tuharrim `alayya reehal jannati waj`alni mimman yashammu reehaha wa rawhaha wa teebaha).

He said: Then, he washed his face and said: O Allah! Illuminate my face on the Day that the faces are darkened, and do not darken my face on the Day that the faces are illuminated (Allahumma bayyidh wajhi yawma taswad fihil wujuh wa la tusawwid wajhi yawm tabyadh fihil wujuh). Then, he washed his right hand and said: O Allah! Give me my Book with my right hand, and immortality in Paradise with my left hand. Judge me with an easy judgment (Allahumma a`tini kitabi biyamini wal khulda fil jinani biyasari wa hasibni hisaban yasira). Then, he washed his left hand and said: O Allah! Do not give me my book by my left hand, and do not bind it to my neck. I seek refuge in You from Hellfire (Allahumma la tu`tani kitabi bishimali wa la taj`alha maghlulatan ila `unuqi wa a`uthu bika min muqta`at al-niran).

Then, he wiped his head and said: O Allah! Cover me in Your mercy, Your blessings, and Your forgiveness (Allahumma ghashini bi rahmatika wa barakatika wa `afwik). Then, he wiped his feet and said: O Allah! Make my feet steadfast upon the Path on the Day that the feet slip off of it and direct my pursuit toward that which pleases You (Allahumma thabbit qadamay `alal sirat yawma tanzilu fihil aqdam, waj`al sa`yi fima yurdeeka `anni). Then, he raised his head, looked to Muhammad and said: O Muhammad! Whoever makes ablution like me and says what I have said, Allah will create an angel for every drop which will sanctify Him, glorify Him, and praise Him; and He will record those as deeds for him on the Day of Resurrection.
